newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea minister seeks Chinese help over defection.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea minister seeks Chinese help over defection.

text.p: South Korea's Foreign Minister will leave for Singapore on Thursday for talks with his Chinese counterpart to try to resolve a diplomatic crisis over a top North Korean official seeking asylum at Seoul's Beijing embassy, foreign ministry officials said.
A ministry spokesman said Yoo Chong-ha would meet Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen at a gathering of Southeast Asian and European officials in Singapore.

Yoo had earlier cancelled his trip to focus on the crisis. South Korea says Hwang Jong-yop, a senior adviser to Pyongyang leader Kim Jong-il, is the most senior North Korean official ever to seek asylum in the country.
Beijing is caught in a wrangle between North Korea, one of its last remaining socialist allies, and the capitalist South which has become an important trading partner and source of investment.
"We are working out a meeting between the South Korean foreign minister and the Chinese foreign minister," foreign ministry spokesman Kwon Tae-myon said.
Other officials, who declined to be named, said Yoo's goal was to enlist Beijing's help in securing safe passage for Hwang to Seoul.
